data_quality.notes: Priority airline gold pass refreshed against British Airways baggage essentials, family baggage, sports equipment, status allowance, seating, and fare-rule sources. Key model: cabin/fare allowance, Basic hand-baggage-only fares, partner operation, and status exceptions.

fees.conditions: One cabin bag and one handbag/personal item are included; cabin bag may be placed in hold if space is limited

data_quality.notes: British Airways guarantees the smaller handbag in cabin, while the larger cabin bag may need hold placement depending on space.

fees.conditions: Checked allowance depends on cabin, fare type, route, status, and whether a partner airline operates the flight

data_quality.notes: British Airways uses cabin/fare allowance rather than a flat first-bag fee. Hand-baggage-only Basic fares are the main no-checked-bag case.

fees.amount: Depends on route, cabin, and booking time
fees.conditions: Basic/hand-baggage-only fares pay for checked bags; price depends on route, cabin, booking channel, and timing
BA Club/oneworld allowances depend on tier and traveler being on the booking; Basic fare exclusions apply

data_quality.notes: British Airways says the status member must be travelling on the booking; group bookings and infants without seats are excluded.

fees.conditions: A single checked bag cannot exceed 32 kg; anything above must be repacked or shipped outside normal baggage

fees.amount: Included if within allowance; extra bag fee if allowance is used
fees.conditions: Sports gear can count as checked baggage if within allowance; extra-bag fee or cargo applies after limits

data_quality.notes: British Airways asks travelers to tell the airline about sports equipment after booking; items beyond size/weight limits must go as cargo.

fees.conditions: Out-of-gauge bags may be accepted up to 190 x 75 x 65 cm; notify BA early and use out-of-gauge drop

data_quality.notes: BA’s oversize rule is handling-based rather than one universal fee; some large fragile electronics must go cargo even within dimensions.

fees.conditions: Advance seat selection is included for First and varies for other premium cabins by fare flexibility and status.

data_quality.notes: BA advises checking the booking because cabin alone does not determine whether advance selection is complimentary.

fees.amount: Depends on route, seat type, and timing
fees.conditions: Advance seat selection fee applies on some Economy fares; pricing varies by route, seat type, and time of selection

data_quality.notes: The live booking or Manage My Booking flow supplies the itinerary-specific advance seat price.

fees.conditions: Eligible customers can choose free from check-in opening 24 hours before departure; Basic is assigned a seat.

data_quality.notes: Basic customers can pay before check-in or accept BA's allocation; changing that allocated seat can still cost extra.

fees.conditions: Change, cancellation, and refund rights follow the purchased fare rules; fare differences and service fees may apply.

data_quality.notes: British Airways does not publish one universal change or cancellation amount across all fares and markets.

fees.conditions: Under 14 cannot travel alone; ages 14–15 may travel alone with required consent and identification documents.

data_quality.notes: BA does not provide a paid escort service; this record models its minimum solo-travel age and documentation rule.
